clue.text: Following star for astronomy, the unknown one in the group

definitions.note: a cryptic definition: put this word after STAR and you get the name of the hobby of astronomy

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the unknown and the one sit within the group

parts.note: a gang is a group of people
algebra's unknown quantities are x, y and z
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An astronomer singles out one mysterious star in a cluster.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a playful one: GAZING placed after the word star gives STARGAZING, a familiar name for astronomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Stargazing is the informal word for watching the night sky, so the missing second half of that compound is what follows star.

clue.text: 16 wants beef and duck

definitions.note: 16 is MARX, so the definition is a member of the Marx family

parts.note: to beef is to complain, and a grouch is a complaint
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Karl Marx is cast as a man who fancies a beef and duck dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: The 16 points to the answer to 16 across, MARX, but here it means the comedy Marx Brothers rather than the philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: Groucho was the moustached, cigar-chomping member of the Marx Brothers comedy team.

clue.text: 16 would mean nothing if pages were replaced by right

definitions.note: 16 is MARX, so the definition is a member of the Marx family

indicators.text: if pages were replaced by right
indicators.note: the clue imagines swapping one set of letters in the answer for another, which would leave a word meaning nothing

parts.note: zero is nothing
R is the abbreviation for right
pp. is the abbreviation for pages

explanation.surface: A gloomy claim that the man would be a nonentity under different circumstances.
explanation.walkthrough: Work backwards: ZEPPO with its PP changed to R is ZERO, meaning nothing. The clue states the swap in reverse of how the solver builds it.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeppo was the youngest of the Marx Brothers, the straight man of the comedy team.

clue.text: Two presents cannot be found

definitions.note: a verb phrase; the answer is an adverb, as in 'it is nowhere'

parts.note: the first present: the present time
the second present: being present means being here

explanation.surface: Two birthday gifts have gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Present has two senses here, the present moment and present in this place, giving two short words; nothing to do with gifts.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is nowhere is absent from every place, so it cannot be located at all.

clue.text: Shining with intellect

definitions.meaning: first meaning: giving out plenty of light

explanation.surface: Describing someone who dazzles with sheer brainpower.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective covers both strong light, as with a lamp, and quick intelligence, as with a clever pupil.

clue.text: Multiple breeder has to go on incessantly

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an animal famous for producing many litters
second meaning: British slang for talking endlessly

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps having children also never stops talking.
explanation.walkthrough: To rabbit, or rabbit on, is everyday British slang for chattering at length.
explanation.definitionFit: The furry animal is proverbially prolific, and as a verb it means chattering at tedious length.

clue.text: Pretentious drinking here? Panic! Lager not quite rum

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the final letter of the word is dropped
rum is old slang for odd or strange, so the letters come out in a strange order

parts.note: taken as written
the beer without its final letter

explanation.surface: A drinker panics in a flashy bar where the lager is barely drinkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like another drink beside gin and lager, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin palace is a gaudily ornate pub, originally a Victorian gin shop, so the place for showy drinking.

clue.text: One mad dog outside that may need clipping?

indicators.note: outside means one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them, which is to tail them

indicators.note: mad means crazy, so the letters beside it are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, then jumbled

explanation.surface: A crazed dog left outdoors probably needs its claws trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' looks like a noun for the pet, but it is the verb meaning to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Nails on the toes grow continuously and have to be trimmed regularly with clippers.

clue.text: Fruit shortage crab turns nasty about

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other
something that turns nasty changes its character, so the letters change their order

parts.note: the two words taken as written, then jumbled
a lack is a shortage

explanation.surface: A crab gets aggressive when there is not enough fruit to go round.
explanation.walkthrough: The word turns is both part of the letters to jumble and, with nasty, the signal to jumble them.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackcurrants are small dark berries grown on bushes and used in jams and cordials.

clue.text: Bird's nest, perhaps, and hence its location?

definitions.text: Bird's nest, perhaps, and hence its location?

parts.note: surface reading: a nest built by a bird, perhaps up in a tree
setter's reading: bird's nest is a Chinese delicacy served in liquid, and a nest found in such a dish is literally in trouble

explanation.surface: A naturalist wonders where a bird's nest might be found.
explanation.walkthrough: Bird's nest is a famous Chinese dish made from swiftlet nests; and to be in the soup is a British idiom for being in trouble, so the nest's location is apt both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Bird's nest is a classic Chinese broth, so it is an example of the dish, and also where such a nest ends up.

clue.text: See 26
Expert collects century at start of play

indicators.note: to collect something is to take it in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: an ace is an expert
a ton is a hundred, a century in cricket

explanation.surface: A star batsman scores a hundred in the opening innings of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture of a century at the start of play is a decoy: play means a stage play.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage play opens with its first act, the opening section of the drama.

clue.text: Ball hit someone

parts.note: to chin someone is to punch them on the chin
someone is a man, an unnamed person

explanation.surface: A ball struck a passer-by.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a chinaman is a ball bowled by a left-arm wrist spinner; the word is now considered offensive outside the cricket sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names a particular type of spin delivery in cricket, so it is one kind of bowled ball.

clue.text: Where some will labour, buxom girl seizes king in his ball

indicators.note: to seize is to grab hold, so the first piece wraps round the other

parts.note: a wench is an old word for a buxom young woman

indicators.note: in places one letter inside the following word

parts.note: the king's ball is his orb, the jewelled sphere of royal regalia
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A bawdy tavern scene: a buxom girl grabs a king at his own ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ball' suggests a dance, but here it is the king's orb, the globe he holds at a coronation; K goes inside it before the whole is put inside the girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A workbench is a sturdy table at which a carpenter or mechanic does manual work.

clue.text: Conclusion of fight to do with Sadat in 50s' conflict

parts.note: a knockout ends a boxing fight
re means concerning, to do with
Anwar Sadat was President of Egypt

explanation.surface: A remark about how Egypt's President Sadat ended a fight during a mid-century war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conclusion of fight' tempts one to take the last letter, but here it is the boxing knockout.
explanation.definitionFit: The Korean War was fought from 1950 to 1953, a conflict of that decade.

clue.text: He co-wrote with 27: "Early bird must switch extremes to sully the vote"

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or sully

indicators.note: swapping the extremes means the first and last letters change places, a reordering

parts.note: a voter marks the ballot with a cross
the lark sings at dawn, and an early riser is a lark

explanation.surface: A revolutionary slogan: the early riser should spoil the ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads first name then surname, but the grid enters the surname first, as in an index. 27 across is ENGELS, so the co-writer is the man behind the Communist Manifesto.
explanation.definitionFit: Marx wrote The Communist Manifesto jointly with Friedrich Engels in 1848.

clue.text: Concert upset the nuts in Northumberland

definitions.note: a prepositional phrase standing for a place in that county

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as at the London Proms

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters go haywire

parts.note: taken as written, then jumbled

explanation.surface: A concert in the north-east of England has driven its audience crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: Northumberland is England's northernmost county; the definition is any place found there, and this is its county town.
explanation.definitionFit: Morpeth is a market town and the administrative centre of the county of Northumberland.

clue.text: As predicted, lunatic hit copper

definitions.note: a phrase; the answer is an adjective meaning predicting

indicators.note: a lunatic is crazy, so the letters go wild

parts.note: the two words taken as written, then jumbled

explanation.surface: Just as forecast, a madman struck a policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman, but it is simply letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Prophetic words foretell what comes to pass, so they turn out exactly as forecast.

clue.text: Work taken up to the rear gate

indicators.note: in a down clue taken up means lifted upward, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: op. is short for opus, a work
the stern is the rear of a ship

explanation.surface: A job is carried round to the back entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A postern is a small back or side gate, especially in a castle wall.

clue.text: Resolve this problem over a narrow strip of land

indicators.note: to resolve is to break up and rework, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written, then jumbled

indicators.note: in a down clue over means turned over, so the word is read upside down

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: A puzzle-setter's instruction to crack a problem concerning a strip of land.
explanation.definitionFit: An isthmus is a neck of land joining two larger landmasses, with water on both sides.

clue.text: Goddess in Sardinia, then East Grinstead

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of Sardinia, the word then, and the start of East

explanation.surface: A goddess tours Sardinia and then a Sussex town.
explanation.walkthrough: East Grinstead is a town in West Sussex; only its first word contributes letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Athene, also spelt Athena, is the Greek goddess of wisdom and patron of Athens.

clue.text: Macerate bananas, scones and jam etc

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters go wild

parts.note: taken as written, then jumbled

explanation.surface: A recipe: soak bananas, then serve scones and jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' sits in the surface as a fruit to soak, but it is the signal to rearrange. A cream tea is a British afternoon tea of scones with clotted cream and jam.
explanation.definitionFit: A cream tea consists of tea served with scones, jam and clotted cream, so the clue lists its parts.

clue.text: See 24
Bird which once landed on the moon?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a large bird of prey

definitions.text: which once landed on the moon?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the name of the Apollo 11 lunar module

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: no bird landed on the moon, but 'The Eagle has landed' was the 1969 message from the lunar module.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apollo 11 lunar module carrying Armstrong and Aldrin was named after the American national raptor.

clue.text: Cocktail wrapped in paper

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a brandy, rum and Cointreau mixed drink
second meaning: enclosed by leaves of paper

explanation.surface: A drink served gift-wrapped.
explanation.walkthrough: The usual sense of the phrase is in bed; here the sheets are sheets of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a classic mixed drink and literally describes something lying inside folded paper leaves.

clue.text: Birds to be shot must be up for it!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: wild birds hunted for sport
second meaning: willing, ready to have a go

explanation.surface: Pheasants about to be shot ought to be willing participants.
explanation.definitionFit: Grouse and pheasant are hunted as quarry, and a person keen to join in is said to be willing and ready.

clue.text: Cocktail sausage cooked: why rave about everything before it?

indicators.note: before it tells the solver to place the second piece in front of the sausage
about can mean all over the place, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: the two words taken as written, then jumbled
all means everything
a banger is British slang for a sausage, named for the pop it makes when frying

explanation.surface: A cocktail-party guest asks why anyone would get excited about a sausage on a stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cocktail sausage' looks like one phrase, but the clue splits after the first word. The jumbled letters give the first word plus the W that starts the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A Harvey Wallbanger is a mixed drink of vodka, orange juice and Galliano.

clue.text: Political philosopher backed member in all quarters but the west

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the second

parts.note: the compass points north, east and south, leaving out west

indicators.note: backed means moved back, so the word reads from right to left

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A politician who has lost support everywhere except in the western regions.
explanation.walkthrough: The compass letters can be ordered any way; they are arranged so the reversed limb fits between N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Engels was a German social theorist and co-author of The Communist Manifesto.
